# Before You File

<p class="lede">A Member of Congress blocked you on X. This packet is everything you need to ask a federal court to make her stop — the complaint, the motions, the order, and the paperwork that goes with them. It is written for someone who has never filed a lawsuit. Read this booklet once, then fill in the blanks.</p>

<div class="note" markdown="1">
**This is not legal advice.** No one has reviewed your facts, and no one represents you. What follows is a set of forms and an explanation of how they work. If you can get a lawyer — legal aid, a law school clinic, a volunteer lawyers' project — do that instead.
</div>

## What's in this packet

| Document | What it does | When you file it |
|---|---|---|
| **Complaint** | Tells the court what happened and what you want | First, with the cover sheet and summons request |
| **Request for Issuance of Summons** | Asks the clerk to issue the papers you serve | With the complaint |
| **Motion to Proceed In Forma Pauperis** | Asks to skip the filing fee, with an affidavit and a proposed order | With the complaint, if you cannot pay |
| **Motion for Preliminary Injunction** | Asks the court to unblock you *while* the case is pending | With the complaint, or shortly after |
| **Proposed Preliminary Injunction** | The order you are asking the judge to sign | With the injunction motion |
| **Certificate of Service** | Proves you sent copies to the other side | After you serve |
| **Opposition to a Motion to Dismiss** | Answers the motion the Member will file | When she files it |

## Start here: four questions

Answer all four before you fill in anything. If any answer is *no*, these forms will not help you.

<ul class="check">
<li><b>Is the account an official account?</b> Look for the Member's title in the display name or biography, a link from her house.gov or senate.gov page, posts announcing votes or committee work, staff-written content, constituent service. A campaign account is not an official account.</li>
<li><b>Were you blocked for what you said?</b> Criticism is protected. Threats, doxxing, and flooding the thread with identical posts are not.</li>
<li><b>Is the Member still in office?</b> If she has left, the block has probably lapsed and the case is probably moot.</li>
<li><b>Are you the person who was blocked?</b> Standing belongs to the account holder. A friend cannot bring this suit for you.</li>
</ul>

## Filling in the blanks

Every blank in the packet is a **fillable PDF field**. Open the file in Preview, Acrobat, or any browser, click a blank, and type. You do not have to print anything to fill it in.

- **Blanks with the same name stay in sync.** Type your name once and every copy of your name fills in. *[[DATE]]*, *[[PLAINTIFF FULL NAME]]*, and the rest behave the same way within each document.
- **Tab moves to the next blank.** Shift-Tab goes back.
- **Save a copy before you start**, so you can begin again if you change your mind about a fact.
- **Then print** on letter paper, one side only, and sign where the forms ask for a signature. A typed name is not a signature on a court filing.
- If you file electronically, most courts accept a scanned signature or a `/s/` signature line. Check your district's rules.

## Five steps to file

1. **Capture the evidence.** *Evidence to capture now*, below, lists what to save. Do it first, because accounts change.
2. **Fill in the complaint**, then the cover sheet, then the summons request.
3. **Decide about the fee.** Pay it, or file the in forma pauperis motion with its affidavit.
4. **File** at the clerk's window or through the court's electronic filing system. Keep a stamped copy of everything.
5. **Serve** the defendants, then file the certificate of service. The case does not start until service is complete.

## The civil cover sheet

Download the court's current **JS-44** from its website. Do not retype it.

| Box | Entry |
|---|---|
| Plaintiff | Your name and address; county of residence |
| Attorney for Plaintiff | Write "PRO SE" and your contact details; no bar number |
| Defendant | The Member, official capacity, office address |
| Basis of jurisdiction | Box 3, Federal Question; check "U.S. Government Defendant"; cite 28 U.S.C. § 1331 |
| Nature of suit | 440, Other Civil Rights |
| Origin | 1, Original Proceeding |
| Cause of action | First Amendment — viewpoint discrimination; right to petition. 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331, 2201 |
| Requested in complaint | Money: No. Other: declaratory and injunctive relief. Jury: No |
| Related cases | None, unless you have filed before about this block |

## Serving the defendants

There is a genuine question whether a Member of Congress is an "officer of the United States" for Rule 4(i) and 28 U.S.C. § 1391(e). Do not bet the case on the answer — serve all four:

1. the **Member**, personally, at her office;
2. the **Member**, in her official capacity, through the **United States Attorney** for your district;
3. the **Attorney General of the United States**, 950 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington, D.C. 20530;
4. a courtesy copy to the **House or Senate Office of General Counsel**.

Certified mail, return receipt requested. Keep the green cards. Rule 4(m) gives you a limited window — currently 90 days — to finish. Put the deadline on a calendar the day you file.

## What you can ask for, and what you cannot

| You can ask the court to | You cannot get |
|---|---|
| Declare that the block violates the First Amendment | Money from the Member |
| Order you unblocked | Punishment of the Member |
| Bar future viewpoint-based blocking of you | An order that she must stay on X |
| Act while the case is pending | Attorney's fees (you have no lawyer to pay) |

Damages are off the table because the Supreme Court has held that the implied damages remedy against federal officers does not extend to First Amendment retaliation claims. *Egbert v. Boule*, 596 U.S. 482 (2022). A complaint demanding damages would be partly dismissed and might be screened out entirely.

## The three arguments you will hear

<div class="qa" markdown="1">
**"It was a personal account."**

Answer with the office's own documents: the website link, press releases pointing to the account, staff-written posts, announcements of official action. The test is not what the Member calls the account. It is whether she had authority to speak for her office and used it. *Lindke v. Freed*, 601 U.S. 187, 198 (2024).
</div>

<div class="qa" markdown="1">
**"It is government speech, not a forum."**

The posts may be government speech. The replies are not: "while the President's tweets can accurately be described as government speech, the retweets, replies, and likes of other users . . . are not government speech under any formulation." *Knight*, 928 F.3d at 239.
</div>

<div class="qa" markdown="1">
**"The Speech or Debate Clause bars this suit."**

The Clause reaches legislative acts, not the operation of a constituent-communications channel. The Supreme Court held that a Senator's newsletters and press release were unprotected because they were not "essential to the deliberations of the Senate." *Hutchinson v. Proxmire*, 443 U.S. 111, 130 (1979). The full answer is in the opposition.
</div>

## What defeats these cases

One federal case was dismissed at the pleading stage against an official who had done everything right from the defendant's side. In *Raven v. Sajet*, No. 23-cv-1251 (D.D.C. Dec. 16, 2024), the director of the National Portrait Gallery had changed her handle to her own name, removed her title and the agency link from her biography, and added "All opinions expressed are my own." The court dismissed because the plaintiff had not plausibly alleged that she "purported to use government authority on her Twitter account."

Three consequences:

1. **Capture the account as it looked on the day you were blocked**, not as it looks when you file.
2. **If the Member has since removed the title or link**, say so and explain what remains official: staff operation, announcements of votes and casework, press releases pointing to the account.
3. **Do not rely on the job title alone.** A title in a biography is evidence. It is not the whole case.

## Evidence to capture now

- The profile page: display name, handle, biography, link, join date.
- The link from the Member's official website to the account.
- Posts announcing votes, committee action, district events, casework.
- The post you replied to, and your reply, each with a timestamp.
- Replies from other users that remain visible.
- The block notice, and the account as it appears to you now.
- Archive captures from the Wayback Machine and archive.today.

Do not crop or annotate. Log the date, time, time zone, device, and URL for every capture.

## If you get stuck

- **The clerk's office** can tell you which forms the court requires and how to file. Clerks cannot give legal advice, but they answer procedural questions all day.
- **The court's website** has a "Representing Yourself" or "Pro Se" page with local rules and a handbook for your district.
- **A law school clinic** near you may take First Amendment or civil rights cases for free.
- **Legal aid** and volunteer lawyers' projects screen for civil-rights matters; ask specifically for a First Amendment or Section 1983 intake.
- **A public law library** — often at the courthouse — has the rules, the forms, and someone who can show you the shelves.

## About the formatting

The filings use letter paper, one-inch margins, 12-point Times New Roman, double-spaced text, a caption block with the court and parties, numbered paragraphs with hanging indents, and bottom-centered page numbers. Check your district's local rules before filing: some require a particular font size, a footer with the case number, or a table of contents for longer briefs. Local rules control.

## A note on the authorities

Every legal proposition in the filings was checked against primary text. Authorities that could not be verified — *Haines v. Kerner*, *Erickson v. Pardus*, *Gravel*, *Doe v. McMillan*, and the text of the Federal Rules — appear only where the filings stand without them. Do not add a citation you have not read.
